query: Why is o365 blocked for columnar, and what are our options?
expected_behavior: Names both nested-inside-nested pairs of the audit stream: ExchangeAggregatedFolders -> FolderItems and ExchangeAggregatedMessages -> MessageItems, with the fields file
Explains that columnar supports only one level of nesting, so the index template PUT fails

Recommends checking that no dashboard or detection rule runs a nested query on the inner path, then mapping the inner level as type: flattened (values kept and still attached to their folder or message; sub-fields become keywords)
Warns that type: group alone is not enough on columnar: the inner objects get detached from their outer element unless the pipeline sends them as dotted keys
Mentions denormalizing in the ingest pipeline as the alternative that keeps per-item pairing, and that the change applies at the next rollover
Shows the exact fields.yml change for each inner field (type: nested -> type: flattened, its fields: children dropped)
Notes that while its only logs stream is blocked the package has nothing to declare, and that the stream can stay on LogsDB with logsdb_columnar: unsupported
Reports threat_response as BLOCKED by nested inside nested, declared as dotted-name sibling entries (whats -> whats.intel_intra_ids, whats.artifact_activity.relevant_actions)
Reports the other five streams separately as READY (endpoint_config's single-level nested field is only a note)
Says the package can declare logsdb_columnar: opt_in once threat_response is marked logsdb_columnar: unsupported
Flags that objects inside the whats and match.contexts elements would be split off on columnar (nested_object_children), even after the inner nested levels are fixed
Does not treat the whole package as blocked

query: Can we declare network_traffic sip columnar-ready?
expected_behavior: Reports the sip stream as NEEDS_REVIEW because shipped detection rules read its _source with JSON_EXTRACT (Potential SIP Extension Enumeration, Potential SIP REGISTER Brute Force)
Explains that columnar _source has dotted keys, so JSON_EXTRACT(_source, "sip.method") returns null and the rules silently stop matching
Recommends holding the stream back until the rules read the mapped fields as columns (COALESCE where the patterns name the field differently), and does not recommend SET unmapped_fields = "load"
Says the fix belongs in elastic/detection-rules

query: What happens to CrowdStrike's lookup indices if the fdr stream goes columnar?
expected_behavior: Identifies the latest_aidmaster and latest_userinfo latest transforms reading logs-crowdstrike.fdr-*
Explains that a latest transform copies the rebuilt, flat _source, so the destination documents get dotted keys
Explains that the destination pipelines' rename processors skip silently on dotted keys, so fields never reach crowdstrike.info.host.*
Recommends a leading dot_expander with field: "*" (or field_access_pattern: flexible) and testing the pipeline with _ingest/pipeline/_simulate

Gives the exact processor for elasticsearch/ingest_pipeline/aidmaster_lookup_namespaced.yml and userinfo_lookup_namespaced.yml, as the first entry under processors:, tagged columnar_*, inline rather than in a separate pipeline file

query: Which aws data streams can go columnar, and which carry the detection-rule testing work?

Points at the exact file and line of the waf nested field (file:line)

query: Can the filestream input package use columnar?

Still lists the informational finding: event.original imported from ECS with doc_values: false

query: Can checkpoint firewall go columnar? What about the packets_dropped field?
expected_behavior: Reports the firewall stream as BLOCKED by event.original's doc_values: false from ECS, which needs no package change and waits on Elasticsearch or Fleet

Explains that packets_dropped is nested and its elements hold objects (source, destination, ...), which columnar indexes apart from their element, so nested queries combining them stop matching and _source splits the elements

Offers the choices for packets_dropped: the dotted-key script processor for the default pipeline (shown as a suggested change), accepting it when nothing combines those fields, flattened, or marking the stream logsdb_columnar: unsupported
Says this looks like an Elasticsearch bug to re-check on newer builds, not a design difference
